title.narrative: Strengthening Life-Saving GBV Shelter Services for Conflict-Affected Women and Girls in Al-Amanah, Ibb, Al-Hudaydah, and Amran

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Yemen Women’s Union (YWU) proposes a seven-month, life-saving emergency intervention to sustain four specialized women's safe shelters. This proposal is particularly timely given the recent UN funding pause, which has resulted in a catastrophic "protection vacuum" across northern governorates. With a 70% drop in specialized services since mid-2025, these shelters now represent the "last line of defense" for survivors. The cessation of shelter operations would leave approximately 300 survivors and 75 accompanying children with no safe alternative, directly exposing them to documented risks of "honor-related" violence, illegal imprisonment, or suicideltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe Yemen Women’s Union (YWU) proposes this intervention to sustain and technically strengthen four specialized Women’s Safe Shelters in the governorates of Al-Amanah (Sana’a City), Ibb, Al-Hudaydah, and Amran. This project is designed as a direct response to the "entrenched protection crisis" identified in the 2026 GBV analysis, which highlights that 56% of Yemen’s population currently requires humanitarian assistance. Since the resumption of intensified hostilities in early 2025, protection conditions have deteriorated sharply, specifically in Sana’a and Hudaydah, where civilian casualties reached a three-year peak of 648 in April 2025 alone. This volatility has systematically eroded traditional community support structures, leaving an estimated 9.6 million women and girls in need of immediate life-saving services.ltbrgtTo address these challenges, the project operates on a survivor-centered, multi-sectoral model, ensuring that women's shelters are not a standalone service but an entry point for a holistic recovery package. Upon admission, every survivor will undergo a rapid protection assessment to develop an individualized safety and care plan. The methodology prioritizes 24/7 intake and case management, legal advocacy to restore rights, and specialized psychiatric care. This is very important because the response has seen a 70% drop in these services since mid-2025. To manage the alarming "protection vacuum" in northern governorates, where 78% of the national GBV waiting list resides, YWU will utilize a vulnerability-prioritization matrix to manage the 367 average survivors needs according to 2024-2025 needs in the four target governorates, including 45 in Sana’a City, 147 in Hudaydah, 113 in Ibb, and 62 in Amran.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe intervention will ensure the continuous, high-standard operation of four safe shelters, providing secure accommodation for approximately 300 survivors and 75 accompanying children. Key outputs include providing specialized psychological and medical help to 300 high-risk survivors, which was an urgent need found in the 2026 analysis. This comprehensive approach ensures that the YWU shelters remain the "last line of defense," preventing tragic outcomes of service gaps, such as the suicide attempts documented among unassisted survivors in the previous reporting period.ltbrgtlt/pgt
